content: 1. After discontinuing medications that act as enzyme inducers, it is recommended to wait at least 28 days before using estradiol valerate/dienogest to ensure contraceptive efficacy. 2. Fluconazole increases the levels or effects of dienogest/estradiol valerate by inhibiting the CYP3A4 enzyme involved in hepatic and intestinal metabolism. Close monitoring is advised, and caution should be exercised. Potential adverse effects include nausea, irregular uterine bleeding, breast tenderness, and headache. 3. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of dienogest/estradiol valerate by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely for adverse effects such as nausea, irregular uterine bleeding, breast tenderness, and headache. 4. HIV protease inhibitors can cause significant changes (increases or decreases) in plasma levels of estrogen and progestin when co-administered. Monitor for adverse effects such as nausea, irregular uterine bleeding, breast tenderness, and headache. 5. Fosaprepitant increases the levels or effects of dienogest/estradiol valerate by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely for potential adverse effects. 6. Fosphenytoin decreases the levels or effects of dienogest/estradiol valerate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Women should avoid using estradiol valerate/dienogest as a contraceptive while taking strong CYP3A4 inducers due to reduced contraceptive efficacy. 7. Gemifloxacin decreases the levels or effects of dienogest/estradiol valerate by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. An alternative or additional form of birth control may be necessary during concomitant use. 8. Gentamicin decreases the levels or effects of dienogest/estradiol valerate by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. An alternative or additional form of birth control may be necessary during concomitant use. 9. Griseofulvin decreases the levels or effects of dienogest/estradiol valerate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Women should use an alternative or backup method of contraception when using moderate or weak enzyme inducers with combination contraceptives. Backup contraception should continue for 28 days after discontinuing the inducer to ensure contraceptive reliability. 10. Dienogest/estradiol valerate decreases the effects of hemin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Drugs that increase delta-aminolevulinic acid synthetase may reduce the efficacy of hemin. Use caution and monitor closely. 11. Hydrocortisone decreases the levels or effects of dienogest/estradiol valerate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Women should use an alternative or backup method of contraception when using moderate or weak enzyme inducers with combination contraceptives. Backup contraception should continue for 28 days after discontinuing the inducer to ensure contraceptive reliability. 12. Imatinib increases the levels or effects of dienogest/estradiol valerate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely for adverse effects such as nausea, irregular uterine bleeding, breast tenderness, and headache. 13. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of dienogest/estradiol valerate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Significant changes in plasma levels of estrogen and progestin have been observed with HIV protease inhibitors. Monitor for adverse effects such as nausea, irregular uterine bleeding, breast tenderness, and headache. 14. Dienogest/estradiol valerate decreases the effects of insulin degludec, insulin aspart, and inhaled insulin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Estrogens and progestins may impair glucose tolerance. Use caution and monitor closely. 15. Isavuconazonium sulfate significantly increases the levels or effects of dienogest/estradiol valerate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 16. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of dienogest/estradiol valerate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely for adverse effects such as nausea, irregular uterine bleeding, breast tenderness, and headache. 17. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of dienogest/estradiol valerate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely for adverse effects such as nausea, irregular uterine bleeding, breast tenderness, and headache. 18. Ivosidenib decreases the levels or effects of dienogest/estradiol valerate through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Consider alternative contraceptive methods, as hormonal contraceptives may have reduced efficacy. Monitor closely. 19. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of dienogest/estradiol valerate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely for adverse effects such as nausea, irregular uterine bleeding, breast tenderness, and headache. 20. Dienogest/estradiol valerate decreases the levels of lamotrigine by increasing hepatic clearance. Combination oral contraceptives significantly reduce plasma concentrations of lamotrigine, likely due to induction of lamotrigine glucuronidation. Use caution and monitor closely. 21. Lanreotide increases the levels or effects of dienogest/estradiol valerate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely for adverse effects such as nausea, irregular uterine bleeding, breast tenderness, and headache. 22. Lapatinib increases the levels or effects of dienogest/estradiol valerate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely for adverse effects such as nausea, irregular uterine bleeding, breast tenderness, and headache. 23. Lesinurad decreases the effects of dienogest/estradiol valerate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Women should not rely on hormonal contraception alone while taking lesinurad. Use additional nonhormonal contraceptive methods. 24. Levofloxacin decreases the levels or effects of dienogest/estradiol valerate by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. An alternative or additional form of birth control may be necessary during concomitant use. 25. Levoketoconazole increases the levels or effects of dienogest/estradiol valerate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely for adverse effects such as nausea, irregular uterine bleeding, breast tenderness, and headache. 26. Lixisenatide delays gastric emptying, which may affect the absorption of oral contraceptives. Oral contraceptives should be taken at least 1 hour before or 11 hours after lixisenatide administration. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 27. Dienogest/estradiol valerate decreases the effects of lonapegsomatropin by reducing serum insulin-like growth factor-1 (IGF-1) response to growth hormone analogs. Higher growth hormone doses may be required. Monitor closely. 28. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of dienogest/estradiol valerate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Significant changes in plasma levels of estrogen and progestin have been observed with HIV protease inhibitors. Monitor for adverse effects such as nausea, irregular uterine bleeding, breast tenderness, and headache. 29. Lumacaftor/ivacaftor decreases the levels or effects of dienogest/estradiol valerate through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Avoid coadministration unless the benefit outweighs the risk. Hormonal contraceptives are not reliable during coadministration. Use alternative contraceptive methods. 30. Dienogest/estradiol valerate increases the levels of maraviroc by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely for potential toxicity. 31. Mavacamten decreases the levels or effects of dienogest/estradiol valerate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Advise patients to use a contraceptive method unaffected by CYP450 enzyme induction, such as an intrauterine system, or add nonhormonal contraception during coadministration and for 4 months after the last mavacamten dose. 32. Meropenem decreases the levels or effects of dienogest/estradiol valerate by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. An alternative or additional form of birth control may be necessary during concomitant use. 33. Dienogest/estradiol valerate decreases the effects of metformin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely. 34. Mifepristone decreases the effects of dienogest/estradiol valerate through pharmacodynamic antagonism. It also increases the levels or effects of dienogest/estradiol valerate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely for adverse effects such as nausea, irregular uterine bleeding, breast tenderness, and headache. 35.
